examples.from: Bengali জল /d͡ʒɔl/ 'water' (cognate; both from Prakrit jala)
examples.note: Assamese has no postalveolar affricates; the letter জ is /z/.

examples.from: Early Assamese জুই jui 'fire' (cf. Bengali জুঁই jũi)
Standard Bengali জাতি jati 'race, kind' (in মানবজাতি 'mankind')
examples.note: Sylheti spirantized the postalveolar affricates to alveolar fricatives (tʃ → s, dʒ → z).

preamble: Deaffrication of the voiced postalveolar affricate [dʒ] to the voiced alveolar fricative [z], losing both the stop phase and the postalveolar place. It is characteristic of the eastern Indo-Aryan languages: Assamese, unique among Indo-Aryan languages in lacking postalveolar affricates and fricatives, has /z/ where Bengali has /dʒ/ (Bengali জল /d͡ʒɔl/ : Assamese /zɔl/ 'water'), and Sylheti spirantized the postalveolar affricates in the same way (dʒ → z).
